newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI DETERMINED TO OVERCOME INJURY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FITTIPALDI DETERMINED TO OVERCOME INJURY.

text.p: Brazilian driver Christian Fittipaldi, who faces at least two months out of action after breaking his leg in a high-speed IndyCar crash, said on Tuesday he planned to return to racing.
Fittipaldi needed a 14-inch metal rod inserted in his right leg after badly fracturing his shin bone in two places during the Australian IndyCar grand prix at Queensland's Surfers Paradise on Sunday.
"If I can be 100 per cent then I don't see any reason why I should not get back into the car," Fittipaldi told reporters from his hospital bed in Queensland.
"Obviously they are not nice memories but I remember everything that happened in the crash," he said.
"I remember I felt a lot of pain when I was being lifted out of the car," said Fittipaldi, whose condition was described as "stable and comfortable" by a hospital spokesman.
Fittipaldi, 26, was injured in a crash at the end of the first lap, forcing a restart of the race, which was won by American driver Scott Pruett.
The crash occured when Fittipaldi's Swift Ford appeared to be bumped from behind in a chicane leading to the main straight and smashed into a side wall, sending debris flying in all directions.
His car was travelling at more than 240 km (150 miles per hour) at the moment of impact and travelled another 400 metres (yards) along the track before coming to a halt.
"Christian will be out of racing for at least two months. I don't think he will be able to drive at all during that time," IndyCar Australia spokeswoman Nan Dwyer added.
"He is hopeful he will be able to leave Australia before the end of the week," she said.

The Brazilian is the nephew of former IndyCar and Formula One drivers' champion Emerson Fittipaldi, who himself underwent a five-hour operation to repair a vertebra fracture after a high-speed race crash last July.
